newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Popularity of future HK leads hits new low - poll.
newsitem.headline: Popularity of future HK leads hits new low - poll.

text.p: The popularity of Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa has hit a new low after his office last week unveiled plans to water down the territory's civil liberties following its return to Chinese control.

In ratings released on Sunday by the Ming Pao newspaper and based on an opinion poll, the rating of Tung's fitness for the job of chief executive dropped by five percent from March to 4.65 points on a scale of zero to 10.
It was the lowest rating since January when the survey was first launched, the newspaper said.
Tung's "trustworthiness" eased by 10 percent to 4.35 points, below the "passing" mark of five set by the poll, which surveyed 803 people, Ming Pao said.

It said the survey was done after Tung's office made proposals on two key laws -- the Public Order Ordinance and the Societies Ordinance, to curb protests and foreign funding for political groups in Hong Kong after the British colony reverts to China on July 1.
The plans drew strong opposition from various political groups, social organisations and the current Hong Kong government, the newspaper said.
Tung's popularity peaked in February when he announced that he would reappoint most of Hong Kong's key government officials to stay on after the transition, it said.
